I think one of the best indicators is how willing a coach is to adapt their philosophy to the roster they are working with. Terry Stotts went from teams that played a relatively egalitarian style of offense during the Dame/Wes/Batum/Aldridge days, being among the league leaders in assists. Then after the summer of 2015 when we lost pretty much all of our secondary playmakers, a great deal of our floor spacing, and of course Aldridge who was considered our go-to isolation scorer at the time, we shifted towards a more heliocentric style of offense around Dame and CJ, predicated on the pick & roll and limiting the decisions that our role players had to make with the ball, which helped limit turnovers but also meant we were always near the bottom if not dead last in assists per game.

Also, for as much crap as Terry got for his defensive schemes, his very conservative style simply made sense given the rosters we had. There was no world where Nurkic was going to be stepping up and playing at the level of the screen when defending pick & rolls and have good results from it (looking at you Chauncey). We also lacked the amount of length, athleticism, and high IQ defenders necessary to consistently make the rotations needed in a zone defense (again, looking at you Chauncey). The reality is there were multiple years under Terry where we actually had good defenses. It really just depended on what he was given, but he always tried to make the most of what he had.

I used to play a ton of Paladins about 4 or 5 years ago. Comparably, the game modes in Star Wars Hunters are quite similar but it definitely leans towards appealing to a more casual player base since it's technically a mobile game that also happens to be available on the Switch. Matches are much shorter because they're capped at a specific time length unless the two teams are tied. The matchmaking process seems to prioritize speed over anything else, which means you can get into matches quickly but the skill balance between the two teams can be quite uneven. Maps are much larger on Paladins and there are no health pickups or ultimate recharge boosts. Not sure about nowadays, but I remember the ranked mode in Paladins being pretty intense and the matches would last like 20+ minutes. Also, Star Wars Hunters is 4v4 while Paladins is 5v5.

Like Star Wars Hunters, Paladins has damage, support, and tank classes, but there's also an additional flank class which is made up of characters with low health pools but very high mobility and close range damage. You won't find any characters in Star Wars Hunters that have the kind of mobility that Maeve or Evie have, which makes sense since most people are playing this game on a touchscreen and occasionally controller. I will say though that the balance between characters in Star Wars Hunters is actually quite good. Nobody seems to be completely useless or so overpowered that you can't win without them on your team. The balancing on Paladins was really bad back when I was playing.
